key_insight: A neural network potential trained on first-principles data can accurately model oxygen-vacancy formation and long-time diffusion in SrTiO3 at scales that are impractical for direct ab initio molecular dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable prediction of defect-driven transport in perovskite oxides, supporting materials design for electronic, ionic, and functional oxide devices.
method: Train an NNP on AIMD/DFT reference data for pristine and oxygen-deficient SrTiO3.
Validate energies, forces, virials, and vacancy formation energies across supercell sizes, including the dilute-limit extrapolation.
Run large-scale, long-time NNP-driven MD to compute vacancy diffusion and Arrhenius migration enthalpy.
evidence_signal: The NNP reproduces DFT energetics and defect trends, and its diffusion coefficients agree substantially better with experiment than conventional classical MD, yielding a migration enthalpy of 0.64 eV versus the experimental 0.67 eV.
watch_item: Performance depends on the coverage of the AIMD training set, so transferability to other defect types, concentrations, temperatures, or strain states should be checked before deployment.
paper_title: Theoretical Investigation of Oxygen-Vacancy Diffusion in SrTiO$_3$ using Neural Network Potentials
